rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 TRADE WINDS BLOW MAP RULES 2 GAME ROUNDS 3 SOLO GAME 4 SCORING 5 NOTES TRADE WINDS BLOW MAP RULES Roll dice to draw lines to take a voyage in your ship. Depending on your ending map location, perform actions or land on islands. Some actions will earn legendary stars. End game is triggered when one or more players earns their third legendary star and one final round is played. GAME ROUNDS 1. One player rolls three six-sided dice (3D6). Each player uses each of the dice exactly once. MODIFY You can modify a dice roll +/-1 by using (exhausting) your sailors. Heroic sailors (with a relic cup) are wild and allow you to choose any (1-6) result. You cannot go above a value of 6 or below a value of 1, but a 6 can wrap around to a 1 or vice versa. Each player has six starting sailors aboard their ship. 2. Players pick two of the dice results to MOVE. MOVE Use one of the dice to set your direction of travel using the corresponding number on the windrose (compass), and then one of the dice for how many spaces you move. You must travel that whole distance unless you travel onto an island space, the DREAD space, or hit the edge of the map. Your ship always travels in a straight line but you may travel through spaces or to islands you have previously visited. 3. Use the last die result to mark off a corresponding square in your Ship’s Duties. If you complete a row and/or a column, immediately claim that reward. 4. Depending on the map location you have ended on, carry out any actions. Your ship does not collect from spaces traveled through or from spaces you've previously collected. 5. Check if end game has triggered. If any player(s) have three or more legendary stars, play one final round and tally scores. SOLO GAME You have sixteen (16) rounds to collect three stars. If you have less than three stars after 16 rounds, you lose. Three or more stars and you win! Tally up your gold as per normal game scoring. Use the outer windrose (compass) spaces to track your rounds. SCORING Islands Visited = gold from visited islands. Printed number on island is gold you receive. Oceans Explored = earn 1/4/9/16/25/36/49 gold for each different unexplored ocean region traveled to or through. Cargo = gold from each piece of sold or unsold cargo. Heroes = earn 2 gold for every ready (unexhausted) heroic sailor. Defeated Dread = gain 14 gold if you defeat the Dread. Living Legend = earn 3 gold for every legendary star. If there is a tie, all players share the victory. NOTES Custom Dice textures designed by Michelle Young

---

Voyages is a roll-and-write game of open sea adventure and exploration. Each player is the captain of a vessel sailing the seas and requires a single printed game sheet and pencil, while one player also needs to provide three dice.

On a turn, three dice are rolled for all the players. Each player chooses one die for the direction they are sailing, another for how far they sail, and the final die for crew duties aboard their ship. Players score points for visiting different islands, gathering and selling goods for trade, and training their sailors in case they come across the mysterious Dread...

Playable from 1-100+ players, either locally or virtually, Voyages will be supported over time with new expansion content provided for free to original backers of the game.

[Rating: 3/10] It's more interesting than most roll-and-writes, but there are still other that I would prefer to play, such as Cartographers, which are quicker, more fun and have a touch of interaction.

[Rating: 3/10] Un Roll-and-Write vraiment sans grand intérêt, beaucoup trop de hasard et le thème n'a aucunement été présent, juste un lancer des dès espérer avoir de quoi qui est pas trop mal et faire avec... 45 minutes pour une partie qui n'en valait pas 10 pour ma part !

[Rating: 4/10] Ranking: :star::star::nostar::nostar::nostar:  A nice PNP roll and write. Nothing spectacular.

[Rating: 4/10] I usually like these roll and write style games, but this one doesn't do it for me. I don't know if it's the artwork or the layout or the mechanics, but there's nothing much here for me that feels satisfying.

[Rating: 5/10] 2 solo games on the "Trade Winds Blow" map and 1 on the "Marauders Reef" map.  I much prefer the Marauders Reef map as it's a little more focused, but that might have a lot to do with the solo gameplay. I think the solo game is going to be different than the multi-player game in that you're more focused on stars than points. Going to islands means nothing, it's all about how you're getting 3 stars. So the first map is a bit too open for my tastes, but the Marauders Reef seems well suited for solo play. Go hunting ships and upgrading duties.  However, I think that puts this game in a tough spot

[Rating: 5/10] The Marauders map is definitely the better solo play option. This is a fine package for the very cheap price, but I do wish there was some element of player interaction for non-solo play. Enjoyable roll-n-write theme anyway.

[Rating: 5/10] Better than some roll & writes, worse than some others. Doesn't overcome the myopic tropes of the genre, but the map on which you maneuver is interesting enough.

[Rating: 5/10] A great attempt at a roll and write with more of a theme and exploration, that leave you with a nice picture of your adventure. But for me it falls into the "That's So Clever" heavier/puzzle R&W style that I don't find that fun.  The main problem I have with it is that with high degree of dice mitigation options that you have, there are so many different choices a player could make that it can be very AP inducing, which I am prone towards.
